products.name: Workday AI
products.note: HR and finance AI; skills-based talent; predictive analytics; sensitive HR data exposure

profile_text.body:
Workday is a publicly traded enterprise software company, founded in 2005 and headquartered in Pleasanton, California, that develops cloud-based applications for human resources, finance, and IT. The company trades on the ticker WDAY and reported revenue of approximately $9.552 billion for the fiscal year ending January 31, 2026.

Workday describes its platform as an enterprise AI system built around HR, finance, and IT workflows. Its primary AI product, listed as Workday AI, incorporates skills-based talent management, predictive analytics, and what the company describes as agentic AI capabilities, meaning software agents designed to find, build, act on, and automate processes rather than only providing recommendations. The site also references an integration with a product called Sana as part of this agentic AI experience.

The held facts show Workday faces a notable volume of litigation, with nine federal cases on record across courts in California, Georgia, Colorado, Maryland, and Virginia, including multiple filings under the name Meckfessel Poletti and cases styled Williams v. Workday, Elias v. Workday, Hill v. Workday, and others. California is identified as the jurisdiction with the highest concentration of legal exposure, with 187 associated entries. Workday files with the SEC under CIK 0001327811.
